Subject: HorizonLock RFP — committed capacity questions

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. We attached the RFP with expected usage patterns (see HorizonLock_RFP_Q3.pdf). A few clarifying items before we schedule a sizing call:

- Current expectation: 1200 active sessions/hour during business peaks (US PST) with an average prompt+response of ~520 tokens.
- Critical SLOs: p95 latency <= 350ms for interactive flows, p99 <= 700ms for batch endpoints.
- We expect to commit to a 12-month reserved slab if SLOs and unit economics (tokens/unit) are in line.

Can you provide a rough tokens/sec estimate for committed baseline vs burst headroom and what the GPU fleet might look like? If you can attach a one-page run-of-numbers we can loop procurement.

Thanks —
Alex Green
Director of Product, HorizonLock

Alex —

Appreciate the RFP. Attaching a quick spreadsheet (redwood_prelim_sizing_v1.xlsx) with baseline math. High-level takeaways up front:

- Baseline tokens/sec (steady): ~5,200 tps (derived from 1,200 sessions/hr * 520 tokens * 60 / 3600 -> math in sheet).
- Peak planning: use 3x burst factor for short spikes -> planning envelope ~15,600 tps.
- SLO fit depends on model variant: for the same quality, a 70B-class quantized variant gives lower GPU TPS than a 20B optimized model. We propose a dual-variant strategy:
  - Commit baseline on an optimized 20B family (q4xx) for predictable cost and higher TPS per GPU.
  - Reserve capacity headroom with a 70B-compatible lane for quality-sensitive traffic, with automated fallback.

Next steps: Kimberly and Priya will drop dimensioning numbers (GPUs, slots, expected p95 mapping) in the thread. If numbers look reasonable we'll produce a canary run proposal and pricing.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Alex / Marcus —

I ran the numbers and sketched capacity options. Putting the assumptions up front so the mapping is transparent:

Assumptions
- Workload: interactive agent flows (avg 520 tokens/request), 1,200 sessions/hr baseline, peak short bursts to 3x baseline.
- Model choices:"redwood-20b-q4" (baseline, ~1.7k tps per A100-80 node with our runtime batching) and "redwood-70b-q4" (quality lane, ~420 tps per A100-80 node). Numbers are conservative — we prioritize p95 latency band.

Sizing options (all numbers in tokens/sec):
- Option A — Cost-optimized baseline: commit capacity for 6,000 tps baseline (covers steady + 15% safety). That requires ~4 A100-80 nodes (4 * 1.7k ~= 6.8k tps). Keep 2 spare on warm standby for short bursts and maintenance -> effective baseline slab = 6 nodes.
- Option B — Balanced commit + headroom: commit 9,000 tps (5+ spare capacity) using 6 A100 nodes for baseline traffic on 20B variants, plus a 70B pool of 3 nodes hot-warm to absorb quality-sensitive requests. Effective peak absorption ~9k + (3 * 420) ~= 10.26k tps before invoking burst throttles. For short spikes above that, we rely on cross-region burst or autoscaling (subject to commit constraints).
- Option C — SLA-first (recommended if p95 <=350ms is non-negotiable across bursts): baseline commit 12,000 tps using 8 A100 nodes, reserve 6 nodes of 70B-class as a dedicated quality pool. This gives a firm absorption envelope ~12k + (6*420) ~= 14.5k tps and keeps p95 headroom.

Latency mapping (observed under Redwood runtime with target batching):
- 20B q4 baseline: p95 ~210–320ms at 1.7k tps/node; p99 tails to ~520ms under load.
- 70B q4 quality lane: p95 ~420–620ms per node; p99 ~900ms+ if cold.

Operational notes
- KV cache warming and prefix caching shave up to 25% off observed tokens/sec demand for repeated prompts — useful for interactive flows.
- We recommend a hybrid rollout: start with Option B + a 30-day canary (10% traffic) to validate token mix and tail-latency. After canary, adjust commit slab or convert warm nodes to hot depending on measured tail behavior.

Deliverables we can provide on short notice
- A fully populated cost and GPU SKU table (price by month) for each option.
- A canary plan (routing rules, alerting thresholds, rollback criteria).
- Contract language suggestions for burst > committed tokens/sec and our fallback policies.

Questions for you
1) What percent of your sessions are multi-turn (avg turn count)? The delta changes prefix cache effectiveness.
2) Do you expect synchronous interactive agents to be highest priority or background batch ranking?

If you confirm the traffic shape we’ll finalize the Option B numbers and hand off to pricing for a formal quotation.

—Kimberly
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
